paper.title: Distributed Multi-Agent Bandits Over Erdős-Rényi Random Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed multi-agent multi-armed bandit with heterogeneous rewards over Erdős–Rényi random communication graphs
unmapped: N agents communicate over a time-varying random graph G_t obtained by keeping each edge of a fixed connected base graph G independently with probability p (not necessarily connected each round)
heterogeneous rewards: the same arm's reward distribution differs across agents
regret measured relative to the global mean reward of each arm (average across agents)
reward distribution class not visible in the provided source (body files missing)
settings.definition_quote: at each time step $t$ agents communicate over a time-varying random graph $\mathcal{G}_t$ generated by applying the Erdős–Rényi model to a fixed connected base graph $\mathcal{G}$ ... where each potential edge in $\mathcal{G}$ is randomly and independently present with the link probability $p$. ... The goal is to minimize the cumulative expected regret relative to the global mean reward of each arm, defined as the average of that arm’s mean rewards across all agents.

algorithms.name: Distributed arm elimination with random gossip

symbols.lambda_G: algebraic connectivity lambda_{N-1}(Lap(G)) of the base graph

source.quote: We theoretically show that the regret upper bound is of order $\log T$ and is highly interpretable... It includes the optimal centralized regret $\calO\left(\sum_{k: \Delta_k>0} \frac{\log T}{\Delta_k}\right)$ and an additional term $\calO\left(\frac{N^2 \log T}{p \lambda_{N-1}(\operatorname{Lap}(\calG))} + \frac{KN^2 \log T}{p}\right)$

results.notes: Only abstract available; theorem body files were not included in source. Gaps Delta_k are w.r.t. global mean rewards. Regret type (pseudo vs expected), horizon knowledge, and noise assumptions could not be verified.
